docs.title: Home
docs.text: The United Republic of Tanzania Ministry of Transport Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority ISO 9001:2015 CERTIFIED

docs.title: Quick Onboarding with CASP
docs.text:
Read this before registering.

The Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority (TCAA) is implementing a programme of continual improvement aimed at modernising its business processes, operational systems and information management — enhancing service delivery, strengthening regulatory oversight, improving operational efficiency, promoting transparency and accountability, and aligning the Authority's services with national priorities and international best practices.

As part of these initiatives, the Authority has introduced the Civil Aviation Services Portal (CASP), an integrated web-based platform that automates end-to-end regulatory business processes across various technical and operational areas. The Portal facilitates online service delivery, electronic payments, workflow and document management, automated notifications, dashboards and real-time reporting. The Authority has also established a 24-hour Customer Service Help Desk for continuous support.

docs.title: 1. Account types — selecting your profile
docs.text:
To maintain regulatory integrity and ensure accurate authority delegation, CASP separates user accounts into two categories. Choose the correct profile during registration:

Organization AccountCorporate / Entity

For all corporate, commercial, private, and government entities requiring regulatory authorization.

Eligible stakeholders:

  • Commercial Air Operators & General Aviation
  • Approved Maintenance Organisations (AMOs)
  • Air Navigation Service Providers (ANSPs)
  • Aerodrome & Helipad Operators
  • Ground Handling Service Providers
  • Aviation Security Organisations & ATOs
  • Government Ministries, Agencies & Departments

Mandatory rule: An authorized Account Administrator must create the entity profile first. Individual staff members must not register corporate or government entities under personal accounts.

Individual AccountPersonal

For individual aviation professionals applying for or managing personal licences, ratings, and permits.

Eligible stakeholders:

  • Flight Crew (Pilots, Flight Engineers)
  • Aircraft Maintenance Engineers (AMEs)
  • Air Traffic Controllers (ATCOs)
  • Flight Operations Officers / Dispatchers
  • Aviation Medical Examiners (AMEs)
  • Individual Rating & Permit Applicants

Personal account note: Always register using your official personal email to retain direct ownership of your professional aviation credentials.

docs.title: 2. Registration prerequisites checklist
docs.text:
1. Active & monitored email address

All official TCAA correspondence, status updates, meeting alerts, GePG payment acknowledgments, account activation links, authentication codes, and verification OTPs are routed strictly via registered email.

2. Valid mobile telephone number

Required for account profile records and emergency contact details.

3. Official registration / identity details

Company incorporation details and TIN (for entities), or Passport/National ID and existing licence numbers (for individuals).

4. Document file format PDF only

All uploaded supporting documentation must strictly be in PDF format. Image files (JPG/PNG) and Word documents will be rejected.

5. Maximum upload size 100 MB

The total combined size of all PDF attachments for a single application must not exceed 100 MB.

6. Stable internet connection

A stable connection is recommended when uploading larger PDF documents, to prevent session timeout.

docs.title: 3. The applicant's journey
docs.text:
A regulatory review pipeline — from registration to certificate issuance.

1 Account Registration Register profile & complete key data fields 2 Electronic Submission Fill application form, upload PDFs, and settle applicable fees 3 Regulatory Review Compliance assessed through document evaluation, demonstration, or inspection where required 4 Licence Issuance Instant online certificate delivery

docs.title: Ready to get started?
docs.text:
Start the full walkthrough → Jump to a specific task ↓ Download the PDF manual

New to CASP? The full walkthrough takes you from creating your account through to managing resubmissions — just click Next at the bottom of each page.

Already familiar with CASP? Skip ahead to the exact task you need below.

docs.title: Quick access
docs.text:
• Getting Started Create your account, complete your first login and profile, or reset a forgotten password.

  • Your Account Update your personal profile, change your password, or manage entity information.

  • Dashboard Understand your Dashboard — applications, licences, notifications, and more in one place.

  • Applications Start a new application, save and resume drafts, or check what a status means.

  • Billing & Payment Pay an application fee via GePG.

  • Meetings Confirm a meeting invitation or view your meeting records.

  • Clarifications Respond to a clarification request from TCAA.

  • Formal Application Respond to a formal application invitation from TCAA.

  • Document Resubmission Respond to a resubmission request from TCAA.

  • Licences & Certificates View and download an issued licence, permit, or certificate.

  • Reference Acronyms, or download the whole manual as a PDF.

Need technical or registration assistance?

The TCAA Help Desk team is available to support you with profile setup and application submissions.

Toll-free support line: 0800 110 193

What's covered right now

This guide documents Core Functions — the parts of CASP common to every regulatory service stream — from the source manual CASP Manual 2026 v01. Stream-specific guides (Airworthiness, Flight Operations, Personnel Licensing, and others) are being written and will be added here. See the source PDF.

docs.title: Change your password
docs.text: Use this when you're already signed in and want to replace your password. If you can't sign in at all, use Reset a forgotten password instead.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. From the Dashboard, click the Profile icon in the top-right corner and select My Profile.

  2. On the My Profile page, click Change Password.

    3. Enter your Old Password. 4. Enter and confirm the New Password. 5. Click Submit Changes.

TCAA's recommendation

The portal advises updating your password at least every three months. If a password is ever compromised, a short rotation window limits how long an attacker can stay inside the account.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Back to Update your profile, or on to Manage entity information.

docs.title: Update your profile
docs.text: The My Profile page is where you manage your personal information and, where your account type includes it, your organisation's information.

docs.title: Open your profile
docs.text:
1. From the Dashboard, click the Profile icon in the top-right corner.

  2. Select My Profile.

The My Profile page is displayed.

docs.title: Update your personal information
docs.text:
1. On the My Profile page, click Edit Personal Profile.

  2. Update the required information on the Update My Profile form — first, middle, and last name, salutation, gender, nationality, mobile number, P.O. Box, physical address, ID number, a copy of your ID, country, region, and district.

  3. Click Update User Profile to apply the changes.

A confirmation message appears once your profile has been updated successfully.

Fields marked with an asterisk are required

The form validates as you go — a required field you've left empty is outlined in red with a message beneath it, and the form won't submit until it's filled. If Update User Profile doesn't seem to do anything, scroll up and look for a red field.

Replacing your ID document

Attach copy of ID shows the file already on record, with a (download) link so you can check what's there before replacing it. Choosing a new file replaces the old one.

docs.title: Other things on this page
docs.text:
• Change Password — replace your password without signing out
  • Entity Details, Entity Attachments, Branches, Customers, Client Employees, Head of Entity, and Account Users — organisation-level records, shown where your account type includes them

What's shown depends on your account type

The My Profile page displays your personal information and, where applicable, the information associated with your organisation (entity). Individual accounts see fewer sections than organisation accounts.

docs.title: Manage entity information
docs.text:
If you registered an Organization account, your My Profile page holds your organisation's records as well as your personal ones. What you see depends on the account type you registered — individual accounts have fewer sections.

Open My Profile from the profile icon, then use the tabs across the top: Entity Details, Entity Attachments, Shareholders/Board, Branches, Client Employees, Head of Entity, and Account Users.

Every tab follows the same layout: a panel on the left with a Note explaining what the section is for and its action button, and the records themselves on the right.

docs.title: Entity Details
docs.text:
Your organisation's registration record: client code, category, TIN, certificate of incorporation and registration numbers, business licence number, contact information, website, location, postal code and address, coordinates, fax, and physical address.

  1. Click Edit Details.
  2. Update the information.
  3. Click Update Details to save the changes.

Three fields you can't edit directly

Company name, Category, and TIN can't be changed from the edit form — a change to any of them may carry workflow and financial implications. Where a name change is genuinely needed, look for a Request Change Name option on the Entity Details panel, which raises a request to TCAA.

docs.title: Entity Attachments
docs.text:
The organisation's supporting documents, listed by attachment type and name.

  1. Click Update Attachments to upload or replace the required document(s).

File rules for entity attachments

Attachments must be PDF, and each individual file must not exceed 50 MB.

Note that this is a per-file limit on the entity profile, and is different from the 100 MB combined limit that applies to attachments on an application.

docs.title: Shareholders/Board
docs.text:
Your organisation's shareholders and board members — name, nationality, percentage of shares, and an ID document.

  1. Click Edit Details to add or update a shareholder.
  2. Click Save.

Shareholding rules

  • Each shareholder's stake must be greater than 0%.
  • Shares accept up to 4 decimal places (e.g. 0.0001%).
  • The shares recorded across all shareholders must sum to exactly 100%.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
Your branch offices, each with a name, contact person, contact details, region/district, and location.

  1. Click Add Branch.
  2. Enter the branch information.
  3. Click Save Branch.

Branches appear on the credential

The branch you select when applying for a licence or certificate is printed on the issued licence document — so add the branch before you start the application, and pick the right one.

docs.title: Client Employees
docs.text:
Employee records linked to the entity — employee number, job title, department, and employment type.

  1. Click Add Employee.
  2. Enter the employee's information.
  3. Click Save Employee.

What this is for

Employees added here can be linked to your account's licence applications and other client operations.

docs.title: Head of Entity
docs.text:
The CEO or manager provided during registration: full name, phone, email, designation, gender, nationality, ID card type and number, and an ID attachment.

  1. Click Edit Details.
  2. Update the required information.
  3. Click Update Entity Head to save.

docs.title: Account Users
docs.text:
Other portal users linked to your entity — name, gender, contact info, address, location, and their identity document.

  1. Click Add User.
  2. Enter the user's information.
  3. Save the changes.

New users must reset their password first

Once a new user has been added, they can't sign in with a password you set for them. They must first use the email address you provided to run the password reset flow, set their own password, and then sign in.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Head to the Dashboard to start an application, or review how to change your password.

docs.title: Save and resume drafts
docs.text: CASP automatically saves your application as a Draft whenever you leave it before submitting. You won't lose any information you've already entered.

docs.title: Resume a draft application
docs.text:
1. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.
  2. Select the Drafts tab.
  3. Locate the application you want to continue.

  4. In the Actions column, select Update Application.

  5. The system reopens your application with its category already selected. Click Next to continue where you left off.

Attachment rules

All supporting documents must be PDF — JPG/PNG images and Word documents are rejected. The combined size of all attachments for a single application must not exceed 100 MB; the remaining quota is shown at the top of the application form (e.g. "100.00 MB remaining").

docs.title: View and download an issued licence, permit, or certificate
docs.text: Once TCAA has approved a regulatory application, the resulting licence, permit, or certificate is issued electronically and made available for viewing and download from your Dashboard.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.
  2. Select either the Licences tab or the Certificates tab.

  3. Locate the required record and check the Status column — it should read Active or Expired.

  4. Under Actions, click the action button for the record and select View Details.

    The same menu also offers Renew and Cancel. Renew only becomes available once a licence has expired — on an Active licence it stays disabled.

    The Application Details window opens for the record.

  5. Select the Certificate tab, alongside Details, Billing, Meetings, Clarifications, and Checklist.

  6. Under Application Documents, click Preview next to the issued document.

  7. In the document preview window, review the document, then click Download to save an official copy to your device.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Back to Application status meanings, respond to a clarification, or to the Dashboard.

docs.title: Start a new application
docs.text: The available service streams, application categories, and sub-categories vary by regulatory service, but the navigation process is the same for every application.

docs.title: 1. Open the application starter
docs.text: From the Dashboard, click New Application.

docs.title: 2. Select a service stream
docs.text:
Choose the regulatory service stream that matches what you need — for example, Airworthiness, Flight Operations, or Air Transport Services.

The tiles aren't in a fixed order

The eight streams don't always appear in the same positions — read the labels rather than clicking by memory or by position. Picking the wrong stream means starting the application again, and once you're past the category confirmation it can't be undone.

docs.title: 3. Review the application guidelines
docs.text:
Read through the guidelines for the selected stream, then choose:

  • Continue with Application — proceed now, or
  • Apply Later — close the guidelines and come back another time

docs.title: 6. Confirm and proceed
docs.text:
Click Next. A confirmation dialog reminds you that the category cannot be changed once you proceed.

  • Review Category — go back and change your selection
  • Proceed — lock in the category and open the application form

Choose carefully

Once you click Proceed, the selected application category is saved permanently and cannot be edited later.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Application not finished yet? See Save and resume drafts.
  • Want to know what each status label means once you've submitted? See Application status meanings.
  • Need to pay a fee before your application proceeds? See Pay an application fee.

docs.title: Application status meanings
docs.text:
The Track your Applications section on the Dashboard shows real-time status for every application. You also receive an email notification whenever a status changes.

Status What it means Not Submitted Started and saved as a draft, but not yet submitted. Submitted Successfully submitted and awaiting TCAA review. Pending Payment Payment is required before the application can proceed. See Pay an application fee. Invited for Meeting A meeting has been scheduled and requires you to confirm attendance. See Confirm a meeting invitation. Invited for Form Submission Additional application forms must be completed before assessment can continue. See Respond to a formal application invitation. Returned for Resubmission The entire application has been returned for correction and resubmission. See Resubmitting the entire application. Form Resubmission Specific documents or sections require correction and resubmission, based on checklist evaluation. See Resubmitting specific documents only. Rejected The application did not meet the applicable regulatory requirements.

You can narrow the list with Filter by status on the Dashboard — see Track your applications.

docs.title: Billing status (separate from application status)
docs.text:
Billing information appears on the Bills page and the Billing tab within an application.

Status What it means Pending Billing is in progress; payment isn't available yet. Billed An invoice has been generated and is available for payment. Paid Payment has been received and billing is complete.

docs.title: Pay an application fee
docs.text:
Certain regulatory applications require payment before processing can continue. CASP generates an invoice and a Government Electronic Payment Gateway (GePG) Control Number for these fees.

The stage at which payment is required depends on the regulatory service and application type. For some applications, billing starts immediately after submission; for others, it's generated only after TCAA's initial review. Watch the application's status and its Billing tab to see when a payment is due rather than assuming it happens at a fixed point — see Application status meanings.

docs.title: 1. Open the billing information
docs.text:
Billing appears in two places: the Bills page in the top navigation (every invoice across all your applications), and the Billing tab inside a single application. Reach the same invoice either through your notifications or by opening the application directly.

Option 1 — Through Notifications

  1. Sign in to CASP.
  2. If the Notifications panel doesn't open automatically, click the Notifications icon.
  3. Select Pending Bills.
  4. Locate the relevant application.

  5. Click View Bill Details in the Action column.

Option 2 — Through Track your Applications

  1. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.
  2. Select the Applications tab.

  3. Locate the application and select the eye (View Application Details) action.

  4. Open the Billing tab.

The Billing tab lists every invoice for this application, with its date, invoice number, control number, amount, and status.

docs.title: 2. Request a GePG control number
docs.text:
1. Select the view action on the invoice to open Individual Bill Details.

  2. If a Control Number is already shown, skip to step 4. Otherwise, click Request Control Number.

    The bill shows its Bill Number, Control Number, SP Code, Bill Date, Bill Expiry Date, Amount Due, Amount Paid, and Mode of Payment, with the line items listed under the Bill Items tab.

    Bills expire

    Each bill carries a Bill Expiry Date — typically about a month after the bill date. Pay before it lapses; the manual doesn't document what happens to an expired control number.

  3. Choose your payment currency — TZS or USD — and click Request CN.

  4. Wait for the Control Number to be generated (refresh the Billing tab if it doesn't appear automatically).

  5. Complete payment through any approved payment channel that supports GePG payments, using the generated Control Number.

docs.title: 3. Confirm payment went through
docs.text: Return to the Billing tab (refresh if needed) — the invoice status changes from Pending to Paid, and your application automatically proceeds to the next processing stage. On Track your Applications, the application status changes from Pending Payment to Submitted.

docs.title: 4. Keep a copy for your records
docs.text:
Once a bill is settled, its Individual Bill Details view offers two documents:

  • Print/Download TCAA Bill — the invoice itself
  • Print/Download Receipt — proof of payment

Receipts are also listed under the Bill Receipts tab on the bill.

docs.title: Respond to a clarification request
docs.text: During application processing, TCAA may request additional information or clarification without changing the application's status. When this happens, a notification appears in the Notifications panel, which opens automatically the next time you sign in.

docs.title: Access the request
docs.text:
Option 1 — Through Notifications

  1. Sign in to CASP.
  2. If the Notifications panel doesn't open automatically, click the Notifications icon.
  3. Select Clarifications.
  4. Locate the relevant clarification.

  5. Click Respond in the Action column.

Option 2 — Through Track your Applications

  1. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.
  2. Locate the relevant application — its status stays Submitted.
  3. Click Action and select View Application Details.
  4. Open the Clarifications tab.

  5. Locate the clarification request and click Respond.

docs.title: Submit your response
docs.text:
1. Review the clarification details.
  2. Enter your response.
  3. Upload supporting documents, where required.

  4. Click Submit Response.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: Your response is forwarded to TCAA for review. A clarification doesn't change the application's status, so keep tracking it from the Applications tab — see Application status meanings.

docs.title: Understanding the Dashboard
docs.text:
The Dashboard is your main workspace in CASP. It opens automatically after you sign in and gives you a single, centralised view of everything happening across your applications, licences, and account.

From here you can:

  • Start new service applications
  • Monitor the status of submitted applications
  • Resume draft applications
  • Respond to actions requiring your attention
  • View licences and certificates
  • Review notifications and pending bills
  • Track application progress
  • Access your account settings

docs.title: Top navigation
docs.text:
The blue bar across the top of every page carries the portal-wide destinations:

Item Takes you to Dashboard This page Bills All invoices across your applications — see Pay an application fee My Meetings Every meeting linked to your applications — see View your meeting records Applications A dropdown of your application views Help Desk TCAA support from inside the portal Bell icon The Notifications panel Profile icon My Profile, entity records, and Logout

docs.title: Dashboard header
docs.text:
The header shows a welcome message and the New Application button, which opens the list of available regulatory service streams.

Selecting New Application displays the streams you can apply under:

See Start a new application for the full walkthrough.

docs.title: Upcoming meeting countdown
docs.text:
When you have a meeting coming up, an UPCOMING MEETING banner replaces the usual welcome message at the top of the Dashboard.

It shows:

  • The meeting title — for example, Meeting for document evaluation
  • The venue — for example, TCAA HQ
  • The scheduled date and time
  • A live countdown in DAYS, HRS, MIN, and SEC

The banner appears only once all three of these are true:

  1. TCAA has scheduled a meeting on one of your applications.
  2. You have confirmed attendance by proposing a date and attendees.
  3. TCAA has approved your proposal.

So if you're expecting a meeting and see no countdown, the most likely reason is that your proposal is still waiting on TCAA — or that you haven't submitted one yet. Check the application's status and the Meetings tab.

The countdown is a reminder, not the invitation

The full details — agenda, venue or virtual meeting link, and any preparation instructions — are in the invitation email and on the application's Meetings tab. See View your meeting records.

docs.title: Summary cards
docs.text: Four interactive cards summarise your account at a glance — Total Applications, Application Status Breakdown, Licences & Certificates, and Quick Updates. Select a card to open the corresponding detail page — see View and download an issued document for the Licences & Certificates card.

docs.title: Track your applications
docs.text:
At the bottom of the Dashboard (or via the Total Applications card), this section lists your applications and credentials in a searchable table. Switch between Applications, Drafts, Resubmissions, Licences, Certificates, and Expired using the tabs.

The table shows the application category, application number, type, application date, current status, and available actions for each record. To narrow a long list:

  • Type in the search box to find a specific record
  • Use Filter by status or Filter by category
  • Sort by clicking the Application Date column header

See Application status meanings for what each status badge tells you to do next.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Click the bell icon in the top navigation to open the Notifications panel, which surfaces items needing your attention:

  • Clarifications
  • Resubmissions
  • Pending Bills
  • Meeting Invitations

Select a notification to view its details and complete the required action.

Check regularly

Delays in completing required actions within the specified timeframes will delay TCAA's processing of your application.

docs.title: Respond to a formal application invitation
docs.text: After you submit an initial application, TCAA may ask you to complete one or more additional forms before the application can proceed — most commonly at the start of the formal application stage. When this happens, the application status changes and you'll receive an email notification.

docs.title: 1. Open the formal application
docs.text:
1. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.
  2. Locate the application with the status Invited for Form Submission.

  3. Click Action and select View Application Details.

  4. Click Form Submission.

docs.title: 2. Complete and submit
docs.text:
1. Complete the required sections of the formal application.
  2. Submit the application for review.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: Your formal application moves on to TCAA for review. Keep tracking its status from the Applications tab — see Application status meanings.

docs.title: First login and profile completion
docs.text:
After you activate your account, you must complete two profile sections before you can use any CASP service: your personal profile, and your entity (organisation) profile.

This is mandatory

You cannot submit any service application until profile completion reaches 100%.

docs.title: 1. Sign in
docs.text:
Signing in takes two steps: your password, then a one-time password (OTP) sent to your email.

  1. Go to the CASP login page.
  2. Enter your registered email address and password.

  3. Click Sign In.

  4. CASP emails a 6-digit One-Time Password (OTP) to your registered address.

  5. Open the email, retrieve the OTP, and enter it on the verification page.

  6. Click Verify OTP.

Didn't get the code?

The OTP screen has a Resend OTP link, which becomes available after a short countdown (shown on the button). Check your spam folder before resending.

Once verified, the system grants access to your CASP profile page.

Forgot your password? Use the Reset Here link next to the password field — see Reset a forgotten password. The sign-in screen also carries a Need help? View the Portal User Manual link.

docs.title: 2. Complete your personal profile
docs.text:
1. Fill in the required personal details — name, salutation, gender, nationality, mobile number, P.O. Box, physical address, ID number, a copy of your ID, and country.

  2. Click Submit Profile.

docs.title: 3. Complete your entity (organisation) profile
docs.text:
CASP also requires a profile for the organisation you represent. This form has four sections: Account Type, Contact Information, Attachments, and Declaration.

  1. Select your Account Type — Individual, Private Company, Government Entity, Foreign Organization, Religious Organization, International Organization, or Embassy.

  2. Complete the required information in the Account Type section, then continue to Contact Information and Attachments, completing all mandatory fields and uploading your organisation's supporting documents. The exact fields shown depend on the Account Type you selected.

  3. On the Declaration section, check Accept declaration.

  4. Click Submit.

The system displays: "Profile submitted. Please sign in again to access the portal."

  1. Sign in again to access all CASP services.

Profile completion is mandatory

You cannot submit any service application until your profile is complete.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Once your profile is 100% complete, head to the Dashboard to start your first application.

docs.title: Create your CASP account
docs.text:
Before you can submit any application to TCAA, you need a Civil Aviation Services Portal (CASP) account.

Before you start

Check the account types and registration prerequisites first — you'll need an actively monitored email address, a valid mobile number, and your official registration or identity details. Choosing the wrong account type (Organization vs Individual) means starting over.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to https://portal.tcaa.go.tz/register.
  2. Enter your email address and create a password.

  3. Click Sign up.

  4. Open the activation email TCAA sends to that address.

  5. Select the activation link in the email to activate your account.

Next step

Once your account is active, continue to First login and profile completion.

Didn't receive the activation email?

Check your spam/junk folder first. If it still hasn't arrived, call the TCAA Help Desk on the toll-free line 0800 110 193 for assistance.

docs.title: Reset a forgotten password
docs.text:
If you've forgotten your password, you can reset it yourself using the email address registered to your CASP account.

Before you start

You need access to your registered email inbox — the reset link is sent there and nowhere else. If you've lost access to that mailbox, call the TCAA Help Desk on 0800 110 193 instead.

docs.title: 1. Request the reset
docs.text:
1. On the Sign In page, click Reset Here next to Forgot Password?

  2. Enter your registered email address.

  3. Click Reset, then click OK on the confirmation.

CASP sends a password reset link to your registered email address and returns you to the sign-in page with a confirmation banner.

docs.title: 2. Set the new password
docs.text:
1. Open the password reset email from TCAA.
  2. Click the password reset link.
  3. Enter a new password.
  4. Re-enter the password to confirm.
  5. Click Reset Password.

The system confirms the reset. You can now sign in with your new password.

Next step

Sign in as usual — see First login and profile completion. Remember that signing in still requires the one-time password (OTP) sent to your email.

Reset email hasn't arrived?

Check your spam/junk folder first. If it still hasn't arrived, request the reset again, or call the Help Desk on 0800 110 193.

Already signed in and just want a new password? Use Change your password instead — you don't need the email round-trip for that.

docs.title: Confirm a meeting invitation
docs.text: Certain certification and approval processes require you to attend a meeting with TCAA during evaluation. When one is scheduled, you receive an email with the meeting date, time, venue (or virtual meeting details), and any preparation instructions.

docs.title: Confirm your attendance
docs.text:
1. Open the meeting invitation email from TCAA and review the details.
  2. Log in to CASP.
  3. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.
  4. Locate the application with status Invited for Meeting.

  5. Click the Action button and select View Application.

  6. Review the meeting details and click Propose Date & Attendees.

  7. Choose a date from the proposed slots, then click + Add attendee to name who from your organisation will attend, and click Submit Proposal.

Who you can add

Attendees are the people from your entity who will represent you at the meeting.

After confirmation, the meeting status updates and TCAA is notified that you'll attend.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
Your proposal goes to TCAA for approval. Once it's approved, an UPCOMING MEETING banner with a live countdown to the meeting date appears at the top of your Dashboard.

No countdown yet? Your proposed date is most likely still awaiting TCAA's approval.

docs.title: View your meeting records
docs.text: CASP keeps a record of every meeting linked to your applications.

docs.title: View meetings across all applications
docs.text:
1. From the Dashboard, click My Meetings.

  2. The My Meetings page lists all scheduled, ongoing, and completed meetings tied to your applications.

docs.title: View meetings for one specific application
docs.text:
1. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.

  2. Locate the application and select View Application Details.

  3. Open the Meetings tab.

This tab shows only the meetings associated with that application, along with their status and details.

docs.title: Acronyms

docs.title: PDF or this site?
docs.text:
Both are drawn from the same source, but they aren't interchangeable:

  • This site is the maintained version. It's searchable, it links related tasks together, and it's corrected as the portal changes. Use it day to day.
  • The PDF is the formal TCAA document, laid out for print and controlled by version number. Use it when you need a fixed, citable copy.

Status of this version

Version 1.0 is marked Release Version.

docs.title: Respond to a resubmission request
docs.text:
During review, TCAA may identify non-compliant documents or request more information. When this happens, the application status changes and you're notified by email to review the comments in CASP and resubmit what's required.

There are two different resubmission scenarios — resubmitting the entire application, or resubmitting specific documents only. Check which one applies to you before following the steps below.

docs.title: Access the request
docs.text:
After receiving the resubmission email, log in to CASP and access the request either way:

Option 1 — Through Notifications

  1. Sign in to CASP.
  2. If the Notifications panel doesn't open automatically, click the Notifications icon.
  3. Select the Resubmissions notification.

  4. Click Update Application.

Option 2 — Through Track your Applications

  1. From the Dashboard, go to Track your Applications.
  2. Open the Resubmissions tab.
  3. Locate the relevant application.

  4. Click Action and select Update Application.

docs.title: Scenario A: Resubmitting the entire application
docs.text:
Use this when TCAA requires the complete application to be revised.

  1. Review the comments and remarks TCAA has provided.

  2. Click Next.

  3. Update the application as required, completing all applicable sections.

  4. Click Next, then check Accept Declaration.

  5. Click Resubmit.

docs.title: Scenario B: Resubmitting specific documents only
docs.text:
Use this when only particular documents or sections require correction.

  1. On the Application Details page, select Go Perform Task.

  2. Review the document checklist and the inspector's comments for each document requiring correction.

  3. Click Resubmit next to the relevant checklist item.

  4. Replace or upload the revised document.

  5. Click Save Section. Repeat for each document identified for resubmission.

  6. After updating all required documents, click Resubmit Form.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
Your application is returned to TCAA for further document evaluation. Track its progress from the Applications tab on your Dashboard until review is complete — see Application status meanings.

Once TCAA approves the application, its licence, permit, or certificate becomes available to view and download — see View and download an issued document.
